title: Modes and Harmonic Minor
description: Same white keys, different home note. Then one raised note that changes everything.

steps.title: Same notes, new home
steps.description:
A mode is what you get when you play a major scale's notes but treat a different note as home. With only the white keys:

• Start on D and you get Dorian. It's minor, but brighter than you'd expect. Lots of funk and jazz lives here.
• Start on G and you get Mixolydian. It's major, with a bluesy, laid-back 7th. Classic rock loves it.

The keys don't change. What changes is the note your ear treats as home.

steps.title: D Dorian
steps.description: Play the white keys from D up to C: D, E, F, G, A, B, C. It sounds minor, but that B gives it a lift. A plain D minor scale would have Bb there instead.
steps.hint: Only white keys, starting on D.

steps.title: Dorian's home chord
steps.description: To make D feel like home, you need a chord under it. Play D minor and then run the scale again in your head. It sits differently now.

steps.title: G Mixolydian
steps.description: Now the white keys from G up to F: G, A, B, C, D, E, F. It sounds major until the F, which is a semitone lower than the F# you'd find in G major.
steps.hint: Only white keys, starting on G.

steps.title: Mixolydian's home chord
steps.description: Mixolydian sits on a major chord. Play G major to anchor it.

steps.title: Harmonic minor
steps.description:
Take A natural minor (the white keys from A) and raise the 7th note by one key, from G to G#. That's harmonic minor: A, B, C, D, E, F, G#.

The G# pulls hard up to A. It also leaves a wide gap between F and G#, three semitones instead of the usual one or two. That stretch is what gives the scale its dramatic, old-world sound, and you'll hear it in classical music, film scores and metal.

steps.title: A harmonic minor
steps.description: Play A, B, C, D, E, F, G#. Slow down at F to G#. Hear that stretch?
steps.hint: All white keys from A, except the last one. Swap G for the black key just above it.

steps.title: Whose notes?
steps.description: D Dorian uses exactly the same notes as which major scale?
